paper_metadata.title: Regime-Dependent Validity in Energy-Flow Cosmology: Evidence from SPARC Galaxy Rotation Curves and the EFC-R Framework
paper_metadata.author: Morten Magnusson

sample.description: Pilot-scale sample spanning diverse morphological types

key_results.description: Correlation between structural complexity (latent field proxy) and EFC performance is statistically significant

pure_efc.label: Pure-EFC (LSB/dwarf)
pure_efc.description: EFC applies without correction; diffuse, low-complexity systems

transitional.label: Transitional (spiral)
transitional.description: EFC partially valid; moderate structural complexity

latent_dominated.label: Latent-dominated (barred/complex)
latent_dominated.description: EFC alone insufficient; significant latent field contribution required

entropy_field_S.description: Normalized entropy, S=0 fully ordered, S=1 thermodynamic equilibrium

latent_field_r_lat.description: Scale radius for latent field activation (kpc)

convergence_notes.FIRE_simulations: EFC-R regime-dependent pattern aligns with independent findings from FIRE hydrodynamical simulations showing non-equilibrium effects in dwarf galaxy evolution
convergence_notes.cusp_core_problem: EFC-R provides principled structure relevant to the CDM cusp-core and diversity problems
